subject: Feature suite unit-econ deep-dive & payback decomposition
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo — unit-econ follow-up (post-call recap)

Hi Julia — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap from our discovery + the items we promised to follow up on so you have everything in one place.

Summary of what we heard (please correct anything I got wrong):
- Primary use: three features across your clinician workflow: 1) SOAP-note draft (long-form summarization), 2) triage assistant (short Q/A), 3) patient outreach messages (templated personalization).
- Current pilot: ~10k MAUs, sample cohort of 300 clinicians.
- Target scale in 12 months: 50k MAUs (conservative), 120k MAUs (aggressive).
- Current average tokens per invocation (we measured from the demo): triage ~350 tokens, SOAP draft ~2,200 tokens, outreach ~220 tokens. Mix today ~45% triage, 35% SOAP, 20% outreach.
- Decision criteria: maintain >40% gross margin on the feature after inference costs; 3–6 month CAC payback target for new clinics; target commercial price target in the range $150–$350 / 1M tokens (you mentioned banding by feature).

Initial unit-econ check (ballpark math):
- Target price band midpoint = $250 / 1M tokens => per-token price = $0.00025.
- Weighted-average tokens per call = 0.45*350 + 0.35*2200 + 0.2*220 = 157.5 + 770 + 44 = 971.5 ~ 972 tokens/call.
- Calls per 1M tokens = 1,000,000 / 972 ≈ 1,028 calls.
- Revenue per call at $250/1M = $250 / 1,028 ≈ $0.243.
- If our delivered inference cost (after batching/caching + quantization) is $0.07 per call (aspirational baseline), gross margin ≈ (0.243-0.07)/0.243 ≈ 71%.

Scenario sensitivity we want to model (we attached a workbook):
- Lower price case: $150 / 1M tokens => rev/call ≈ $0.146.
- Higher tokens assumption (20% more tokens) => rev/call unchanged, cost/call increases proportionally.
- Quantization / perf wins: expected cost reduction 1.8–3x depending on model variant + caching.

Immediate asks / open items for you:
1) Can you confirm expected MAU tier you want us to model (50k conservative vs 120k aggressive)?
2) FYI we attached the unit_econ workbook that has three tabs: assumptions, per-feature breakdown, payback timeline. Please drop your real numbers in the green fields and we’ll produce an updated model.
3) If you have historical average token-per-invocation per feature (CSV) that would speed up a more accurate run.
4) Suggested next step: 60-minute unit-econ deep-dive w/ pricing + tech (we’d bring Karthik to discuss caching/quantization impacts). We’re proposing Thu 4/15 10:00–11:00 PT.

Attachments: clarity_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), call-recording-20270412.mp3 (recording).

Thanks — will follow up once you drop numbers into the sheet.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Julia Park <julia@clarityhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Clarity Health Procurement <procurement@clarityhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo — unit-econ follow-up (post-call recap)

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear write-up and the workbook. A few clarifications and our requested inputs:

Corrections / confirmations:
- Pilot is 10k MAUs but active clinician seats in pilot = 320 (minor correction).
- Usage pattern: the triage assistant is the highest-frequency (we'll be using it inside clinician workflow), SOAP drafts are heavier but used per patient encounter (~1 per encounter).

Numbers I've pasted into your workbook (tab: assumptions):
- Current MAUs: 10,000 (pilot); Projection (12mo conservative): 55,000; Projection aggressive: 130,000.
- Avg feature usage per MAU/month: 3.2 triage calls, 0.8 SOAP drafts, 4 outreach messages.
- Tokens per call (sampled median): triage 320, SOAP 1,900, outreach 240.

Commercial notes from procurement:
- Clarity's procurement target: payback <= 4 months on average for new clinic acquisition.
- Desired margin floor per feature: >= 45% after inference and variable costs.
- Budget envelope: preliminary pilot budget ~$25k/month, scaling to $120k/month at 55k MAUs (expected spend range 120–350k/month at 130k MAUs depending on opt-in rate).

We uploaded an anonymized token log for April to the Drive link you shared — file: clarity_token_sample_apr.csv. Please confirm you can access it.

We can do the deep-dive Thu 4/15 10:00 PT — Karthik joining sounds good. Will your team include someone from tech performance?

Best,
Julia
Julia Park
Head of Product, Clarity Health
julia@clarityhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Clarity Health Procurement <procurement@clarityhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo — unit-econ follow-up (post-call recap)

Perfect — got the CSV, thanks. I updated the assumptions tab to reflect the MAU and usage numbers you pasted and ran two quick scenarios in the attached workbook (conservative vs aggressive). High-level observations:

1) Conservative (55k MAU, current opt-in estimates):
- Estimated monthly token consumption: ~210M tokens.
- If we price at $250 / 1M tokens => revenue run-rate ~ $52.5k/month; estimated inference cost (with baseline optimizations) ≈ $14k/month => gross margin ~ 73% (well above the 45% floor).
- CAC payback: with your stated pilot CAC approx $1,200/clinic and ARPU per clinic ≈ $700/month under conservative adoption, payback ≈ 1.7 months (good).

2) Aggressive (130k MAU):
- Tokens: ~520M tokens/month.
- At $200 / 1M tokens (we recommend tiered pricing) => revenue ≈ $104k/month; cost ≈ $36k/month => gross margin ~65%.
- With caching and 2.5x quant improvement (aggressive infra), cost could drop to ~$14k => margin >80%.

Risk notes to flag to your team:
- SOAP drafts dominate token volume; even small reductions in prompt length (templating + structured inputs) reduce total spend significantly; we can run a prompt-compression pilot to aggressively cut SOAP tokens by 20–30%.
- If Clarity needs a $150/1M price to hit procurement targets, margin compresses and we'd recommend either higher adoption (spread CAC) or limiting SOAP draft length.

I've attached the workbook with the scenarios labeled. For the call Thu we will:
- Walk the model line-by-line;
- Show cache + quantization sensitivity;
- Propose pricing bands (pilot, scale A, scale B) and suggested SLA/tier tradeoffs.

See you Thu 4/15 10:00 PT. I'll kick off a calendar invite shortly and include the call recording + workbook.

—Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Julia Park <julia@clarityhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick demo — unit-econ follow-up (post-call recap)

Quick technical notes to prep the deep-dive:
- Caching: for SOAP drafts we can cache clinician-specific prefixes (patient demographic prompts, templates). If templates are normalized we typically see ~18–28% token reduction for heavy templated drafts.
- Quantization: recommending int8/llm.int8 or 4-bit hybrid for the balance of perf and quality. Expect 2–3x inference cost reduction vs fp16 on supported variants. We’ll validate on your April sample before finalizing numbers.
- Batching/Autoscaling: batching at request level will lower cost per token but increases tail latency; given your SLA (~<300ms tail for triage), we’ll assume conservative batching (small batch sizes) for triage and larger batching windows for offline SOAP draft queueing.
- Implementation ask for pilot: a 1-week A/B prompt compression pilot (we’ll instrument token delta side-by-side) + run quantized evaluation on a 500-sample SOAP set.

I’ll prepare a one-slide summary of these levers for Thu’s call and populate the workbook with backend cost assumptions (we included ranges: best/expected/worst).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving & Performance, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — great call. Notes / agreed next steps: 
1) Redwood: run the quantization + token-compression pilots (1 week) and return a validated per-feature cost table. Deliverable: updated workbook + a 1-pager summary. ETA: 4/22.
2) Clarity: confirm which clinics are in scope for the pilot (we need a sample of 5 clinics) and share the sanitized 2-week token log (you already shared April sample — thanks).
3) Commercial: we’ll draft a tiered pricing strawman (pilot rate, scale A, scale B) tied to monthly token buckets and commit levels; Ben will circulate a draft before EOD 4/20.
4) Legal / Procurement: Julia, procurement asked about NDA / data processing addendum — Ben will loop in legal (we’ll attach our DPA + SOC2 summary to the deal record).

Action items owner list (in workbook): Ben (pricing strawman, call recording), Karthik (pilot knobs + cost assumptions), Marissa (commercial comps + competitive notes), Julia (pilot clinics + sanitized logs).

Open questions for your team: are you comfortable with a pilot commit of ~$25k/month budgeted? If not, tell us target cap and we’ll re-scope pilot features to hit budget.

Thanks — calendared follow-up for 4/22 to review validated numbers.

—Ben
